candidate: build fast path in front of the loaded-library cache (hipengine/core/build.py)
reason: iteration 24's launch census found ~14 tiny elementwise launches per layer per decode step (~420/step before any GEMM) and attributed the 8.0 ms/token host gap measured in iteration 19 to them. Decomposing the per-launch host cost found the gap was not in the HIP call: a bare ctypes call with prebuilt args costs 1.84 us, signed_kernel_fn 0.53 us, but the launcher wrapper cost 11.81 us. The extra ~9.5 us was build_hip re-deriving its cache key on every launch, because the kernel launchers resolve their library per call (they pass no library= kwarg): build_gemma4_norm(load=True) alone measured 7.97 us, of which _resolve_compiler_version was 2.05, the target-arch read 0.85, cache-root resolution 0.48, os.fspath/Path normalisation ~2.2, and the rest call glue. os.environ.get costs 0.463 us per read on POSIX because the mapping fsencodes the key on every access, so the 8-12 environment reads in the derivation were the largest single term.

mechanism.diagnosis: per-launch library resolution, not the HIP launch itself, dominated host launch cost
mechanism.cause: build_hip computed its cache key - compiler version probe, target-arch read, cache-root resolution and path normalisation - before consulting _LOADED_LIB_CACHE, so a repeated identical per-launch load paid ~8 us of key derivation for a dict lookup
mechanism.fix: _FAST_PATH_CACHE in front of the loaded-library cache, keyed on the raw request (family, profile, output_name, os.fspath(sources), cache_root, compiler, compiler_version, target_arch, os.fspath(include_dirs), extra_flags) plus _build_env_signature(compiler). os.fspath rather than str(Path(...)) because the latter re-parses the path (~2 us) and is the second largest term being removed.
mechanism.environment_soundness: _BUILD_ENV_KEYS lists every knob the key derivation or the flag builders read (cache root, both arch vars, require_cached, both device-lib-path vars, HIPENGINE_PREFILL_MCUMODE, HIPENGINE_DISABLE_UNROLL600), plus the four version-override variables via _environment_version_identity. A mid-process environment change therefore selects a fresh resolution instead of a stale library, which is the contract _LOADED_LIB_CACHE already had.
mechanism.cheap_environment_reads: _env_get and _build_env_signature read the bytes-keyed dict behind os.environ (_ENVIRON_DATA, shared with os.environb) with precomputed byte keys instead of the public mapping, and fall back to os.environ.get whenever CPython does not expose that dict or a caller has swapped os.environ for another object. Both paths observe in-place mutations, so the response to environment changes is unchanged. _version_env_keys_bytes caches the four per-compiler version keys so the f-string construction is not repeated per launch.

performance.interpretation: the gain scales inversely with per-step GPU work (+7.2% at 128p, +1.7% at 512p, +0.8% at 1024p, flat at 4096p), which is the signature of host dispatch time that is hidden behind GPU execution at long prompts and exposed at short ones. This closes iteration 19's host-gap hypothesis as a critical-path item at the campaign's primary row: removing 6.4 ms/token of host time moved 1024p by +0.8%, so the remaining step time there is GPU work.
